messages:
sara: FYI ACME reported embeddings throughput drop after yesterday's batching config change. tokens/sec looks normal but vectors/sec down ~60% for their workload. ticket: INC-4827

mike: thanks — do we have a repro or customer request payload?

sara: minimal repro in prod hitting /v1/embeddings. small batch of 8 docs. curl included below. it used to return ~1.2k vecs/sec, now ~480.

sara: ```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"embed-xl-2025","inputs":["...","..."]}'
```

raj: looking at infra metrics — GPU util per-slot is high (90%+) and paired with long queue depths on the vectorizer service. interestingly, token generation pipeline (text path) has normal latency. suggests KV cache or batching-related head-of-line.

infra-bot: autoscaler event at 3034998000: scale_down_blocked due to pending_kv_locks > 12, pending_requests=340 

mike: can you paste the kvcache trace? we changed batch_window_ms from 25 -> 8 in rollout v2, right?

raj: yes. here's a short excerpt from the kvcache log span showing contention: 

```
[kvcache] 3035000101 LOCK_WAIT pid=3421 key=kv-embed-64ms wait_ms=72
[kvcache] 3035000101 LOCK_WAIT pid=3425 key=kv-embed-64ms wait_ms=88
[vectorize] 3035000110 batch_size=3 latency_ms=1120 queue_len=46
[gpu-queue] 3035000112 enqueue_delay_ms=210 headload=18
```

emma: also saw auth:billing retries for ACME around the same time but only a handful of 401->200 retries. unlikely majority cause but worth noting.

sara: customer said they switched to our new batching sample in their SDK which adds extra small requests. Could be many small batches hitting same hot shard.

mike: hypothesis: shorter batch window produced more very-small batches; increased per-batch overhead and more kvcache key contention (hot prefixes). tokens/sec stable because token path is sharded differently; vectorization uses a smaller number of hot model replicas.

raj: agreed. I ran a quick A/B on a staging customer by reverting batch_window_ms to 25ms and throughput jumped back ~+70%. logs: batch sizes moved from median 4 -> 16 and kvcache wait went down.

ops: what about fallback to embed-medium until we fix? lower quality but cheaper. will customer accept temporary fallback?

sara: ACME prefers no quality loss. they asked for immediate mitigation without model change.

mike: plan: 1) rollback batch_window_ms to 25ms for the routing pool handling ACME (hotfix) 2) increase kvcache mutex pool and reduce per-key serialization 3) add autoscaler rule to cap pending_kv_locks before scale down 4) run a canary of batch_window=12 with K/V mutex changes before global rollout.

raj: I've queued a config rollback PR and bumped kvcache parallelism on the hot shard. rolling to three replicas now. monitoring dashboards: vector/sec, median batch size, kvcache_wait_ms, gpu_queue_depth.

infra-bot: deployment 3035000205: config-revert batch_window_ms=25 targeting pool=embeddings-hot (3 replicas).

sara: testing with ACME customer now — they report vectors/sec improving to ~900 and errors down. continuing to watch.

mike: follow-ups: add a postmortem note to INC-4827, capture SDK batch patterns that create small-size bursts, and add unit test for kvcache hot-prefix distribution. assign to raj + devex.

emma: filing a billing/auth follow-up to verify retries didn't amplify traffic; ticket BIL-1102.

sara: thanks team. I'll ping if ACME sees anything else. :thumbsup:
